image_prompt.text: Treadmills you run on to build speed, packed densely enough across every level that a player is always standing on one
A wall between each level that only opens once you are fast enough, each one demanding more speed than the one before it
A starting zone at the bottom of the ladder where speed upgrades are bought before setting off

layout_placement.text: Treadmill stations that raise the speed stat while a player runs on them
A pad at the far end of the tenth level that trades all speed for a permanent multiplier

mechanics: A '1+ speed' stat that goes up as you play
Ten levels, and every level gets harder the further you go
Running on a treadmill gets you more speed
notes: Classified as the Simulation '+1 speed' family: the prompt self-declares '1+ speed obby', and the genre note says the stat is the game, so Simulation leads on tier-ladder at P0 and obby-platformer is named second without importing its genre-wide P6.

Did not take obby's path-track, which would have carried P6: the Simulation note says a stat ladder's geometry is just ground and nothing has to be validated. If the ten levels really are jump courses this is the wrong call and the build needs P6.
The run's end was inferred rather than asked: trigger-rebirth sits at the far end of the last tier, per the Stat Grinder preset.
The prompt's '10 levels' is a property of the shape, which has no count field, so the number is carried as count: 10 on gate-progression (one wall per level) to keep it from being lost.
Stat Grinder taken whole. social-hub and trigger-rebirth come from the preset, not from anything the user said.
Scale assumed block: a strict reading of 'the detail wins' points at room, since treadmills are prop-scale, but ten tiers do not fit under 100 studs.

open_questions.ask: When you say each of the ten levels gets harder, do you mean the jumping gets harder — bigger gaps, moving platforms, things that kill you on contact — or that the ground stays flat and the only thing stopping you is a barrier that needs more speed than you have yet?
Are the ten levels laid out end to end as one continuous run you keep climbing through, or is each level its own separate area you get sent to?
How should it look — bright and cartoony, sleek neon sci-fi, or a plain gym/training-facility look?

captured: ten levels as ten tiers in a ladder
difficulty rising level by level, expressed as progressively harder speed gates
treadmills you run on for speed

skill_gap.name: shape carries no count
skill_gap.why: '10 levels' is the one number in the prompt and it is a property of tier-ladder, but shape has no count field, so it only survives by being hung on gate-progression — which counts walls, not levels

notes_for_us: Genre files give Typical shapes as bare IDs, so shape.type and shape.name cannot be filled for tier-ladder without loading shapes.md, which step 2 tells you not to do by default. Emitted both as null.

Simulation's '+1 speed' note says these stay P0, but the prompt says 'obby' and obby's own path-track carries P6. Nothing says whether an option-level P6 imported from the secondary genre counts as the genre-wide P6 the note forbids.

Scale is unresolvable as written: 'the detail wins' points at room because treadmills are prop-scale, but ten tiers cannot fit under 100 studs, and the trigger for asking is an extent with no contents — the opposite of this prompt.
gate-progression is both prompt-implied (ten levels need separating) and a Stat Grinder option, and no rule says which side of preset_derived that lands on. Counted as prompt-derived.
This item in prompts.json has no 'enriched' key, so coverage.enriched_invented cannot be filled at all.
